name: Wang Wei
credit: Portrait: unknown artist — Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Wang Wei (AD 699–759) was a T’ang poet, painter and devout Buddhist, famous for quiet poems of landscape and friendship.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Overlooked
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Herbert A. Giles (1898)

poems.title: Goodbye
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Herbert A. Giles (1898)
poems.text:
We parted at the gorge and cried "Good cheer!"
The sun was setting as I closed my door;
Methought, the spring will come again next year,
But he may come no more.

poems.title: A Rencontre
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Herbert A. Giles (1898)
poems.text:
Sir, from my dear old home you come,
And all its glories you can name;

Oh tell me, — has the winter-plum
Yet blossomed o'er the window-frame?

poems.title: Goodbye to Meng Hao-jan
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Herbert A. Giles (1898)
poems.text:
Dismounted, o'er wine we had said our last say;
Then I whisper, "Dear friend, tell me whither away."
"Alas!" he replied, "I am sick of life's ills
"And I long for repose on the slumbering hills.
" But oh seek not to pierce where my footsteps may stray:
"The white clouds will soothe me for ever and ay."

poems.title: After an Imperial Audience at Dawn in the "Palace of Great Brilliance"
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.note: Full heading in the book: "Written by Wang Wei, in the manner of Chia, the (Palace) Secretary, after an imperial audience at dawn in the 'Palace of Great Brilliance'."
poems.translator: trans. Florence Ayscough and Amy Lowell (1921)
poems.text:
At the first light of the still-concealed sun, the Cock-man, in his dark-red cap, strikes the tally-sticks and proclaims aloud the hour.
At this exact moment, the Keeper of the Robes sends in the eider-duck skin dress, with its cloud-like curving feather-scales of kingfisher green.
In the Ninth Heaven, the Ch'ang Ho Gate opens; so do those of the Palaces, and the Halls of Ceremony in the Palaces.
The ten thousand kingdoms send their ambassadors in the dresses and caps of their ranks to do reverence before the pearl-stringed head-dress.
The immediately-arrived sun tips the "Immortal Palm"; it glitters.
Sweet-scented smoke rises and flows about the Emperor's ceremonial robes, making the dragons writhe.
The audience ended, I wish to cut the paper of five colours and write upon it the words of the Son of Heaven.
My jade girdle-ornaments clash sweetly as I return to sit beside the Pool of the Crested Love-Pheasant.

poems.title: The Blue-green Stream
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Florence Ayscough and Amy Lowell (1921)
poems.text:
Every time I have started for the Yellow Flower River,
I have gone down the Blue-Green Stream,
Following the hills, making ten thousand turnings.
We go along rapidly, but advance scarcely one hundred li.
We are in the midst of a noise of water,
Of the confused and mingled sounds of water broken by stones,
And in the deep darkness of pine-trees.
Rocked, rocked,
Moving on and on,
We float past water-chestnuts
Into a still clearness reflecting reeds and rushes.
My heart is clean and white as silk; it has already achieved Peace;
It is smooth as the placid river.
I long to stay here, curled up on the rocks,
Dropping my fish-line forever.

poems.title: Farm House on the Wei Stream
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Florence Ayscough and Amy Lowell (1921)
poems.text:
The slanting sun shines on the cluster of small houses upon the heights.
Oxen and sheep are coming home along the distant lane.
An old countryman is thinking of the herd-boy,
He leans on his staff by the thorn-branch gate, watching.
Pheasants are calling, the wheat is coming into ear,
Silk-worms sleep, the mulberry-leaves are thin.
Labourers, with their hoes over their shoulders, arrive;
They speak pleasantly together, loth to part.
It is for this I long--unambitious peace!
Disappointed in my hopes, dissatisfied, I hum "Dwindled and Shrunken."

poems.title: While Roses Fall
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. L. Cranmer-Byng (1916)
poems.text:
Dawn after dawn the last doth nearer bring.
Ah! what avails the shy return of spring?
Then fill the wine-cup of to-day and let
Night and the roses fall, while we forget.

poems.title: Deer-Park Hermitage
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
There seems to be no one on the empty mountain . . .
And yet I think I hear a voice,
Where sunlight, entering a grove,
Shines back to me from the green moss.

poems.title: In a Retreat Among Bamboos
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Leaning alone in the close bamboos,
I am playing my lute and humming a song
Too softly for anyone to hear —
Except my comrade, the bright moon.

poems.title: A Parting
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Friend, I have watched you down the mountain
Till now in the dark I close my thatch door. . . .
Grasses return again green in the spring,
But O my Prince of Friends, do you?

poems.title: One-Hearted
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
When those red berries come in springtime,
Flushing on your southland branches,
Take home an armful, for my sake,
As a symbol of our love.

poems.title: Lines
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
You who have come from my old country,
Tell me what has happened there! —
Was the plum, when you passed my silken window,
Opening its first cold blossom?

poems.title: On the Mountain Holiday
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.note: Thinking of My Brothers in Shan-tung
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
All alone in a foreign land,
I am twice as homesick on this day
When brothers carry dogwood up the mountain,
Each of them a branch — and my branch missing.

poems.title: A Song at Wei-ch'eng
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
A morning-rain has settled the dust in Wei-ch'eng;
Willows are green again in the tavern dooryard. . . .
Wait till we empty one more cup —
West of Yang Gate there'll be no old friends.

poems.title: A Song of an Autumn Night
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Under the crescent moon a light autumn dew
Has chilled the robe she will not change —
And she touches a silver lute all night,
Afraid to go back to her empty room.

poems.title: A Message from My Lodge at Wang-ch'uan
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
The mountains are cold and blue now
And the autumn waters have run all day.
By my thatch door, leaning on my staff,
I listen to cicadas in the evening wind.
Sunset lingers at the ferry,
Supper-smoke floats up from the houses.
. . . Oh, when shall I pledge the great Hermit again
And sing a wild poem at Five Willows?

poems.title: An Autumn Evening in the Mountains
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
After rain the empty mountain
Stands autumnal in the evening,
Moonlight in its groves of pine,
Stones of crystal in its brooks.
Bamboos whisper of washer-girls bound home,
Lotus-leaves yield before a fisher-boat —
And what does it matter that springtime has gone,
While you are here, O Prince of Friends?

poems.title: Bound Home to Mount Sung
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
The limpid river, past its bushes
Running slowly as my chariot,
Becomes a fellow voyager
Returning home with the evening birds.
A ruined city-wall overtops an old ferry,
Autumn sunset floods the peaks.
. . . Far away, beside Mount Sung,
I shall close my door and be at peace.

poems.title: Mount Chung-nan
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Its massive height near the City of Heaven
Joins a thousand mountains to the corner of the sea.
Clouds, when I look back, close behind me,
Mists, when I enter them, are gone.
A central peak divides the wilds
And weather into many valleys.
. . . Needing a place to spend the night,
I call to a wood-cutter over the river.

poems.title: Answering Vice-Prefect Chang
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
As the years go by, give me but peace,
Freedom from ten thousand matters.
I ask myself and always answer:
What can be better than coming home?
A wind from the pine-trees blows my sash,
And my lute is bright with the mountain moon.
You ask me about good and evil fortune? . . .
Hark, on the lake there's a fisherman singing!

poems.title: Toward the Temple of Heaped Fragrance
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Not knowing the way to the Temple of Heaped Fragrance,
Under miles of mountain-cloud I have wandered
Through ancient woods without a human track;
But now on the height I hear a bell.
A rillet sings over winding rocks,
The sun is tempered by green pines. . . .
And at twilight, close to an emptying pool,
Thought can conquer the Passion-Dragon.

poems.title: A Message to Commissioner Li at Tsu-chou
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
From ten thousand valleys the trees touch heaven;
On a thousand peaks cuckoos are calling;
And, after a night of mountain rain,
From each summit come hundreds of silken cascades.
. . . If girls are asked in tribute the fibre they weave,
Or farmers quarrel over taro fields,
Preside as wisely as Wen-weng did. . . .
Is fame to be only for the ancients?

poems.title: A View of the Han River
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
With its three southern branches reaching the Ch'u border,
And its nine streams touching the gateway of Ching,
This river runs beyond heaven and earth,
Where the colour of mountains both is and is not.
The dwellings of men seem floating along
On ripples of the distant sky —
These beautiful days here in Hsiang-yang
Make drunken my old mountain heart!

poems.title: My Retreat at Mount Chung-nan
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
My heart in middle age found the Way,
And I came to dwell at the foot of this mountain.
When the spirit moves, I wander alone
Amid beauty that is all for me. . . .
I will walk till the water checks my path,
Then sit and watch the rising clouds —
And some day meet an old wood-cutter
And talk and laugh and never return.

poems.title: An Early Audience at the Palace of Light
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)

poems.title: Looking Down in a Spring Rain on the Course from Fairy-Mountain Palace to the Pavilion of Increase
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)

poems.title: In My Lodge at Wang-ch'uan After a Long Rain
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
The woods have stored the rain, and slow comes the smoke
As rice is cooked on faggots and carried to the fields;
Over the quiet marsh-land flies a white egret,
And mango-birds are singing in the full summer trees. . . .
I have learned to watch in peace the mountain morning-glories,
To eat split dewy sunflower-seeds under a bough of pine,
To yield the post of honour to any boor at all . . .
Why should I frighten sea-gulls, even with a thought?

poems.title: Harmonizing a Poem by Palace-Attendant Kuo
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
High beyond the thick wall a tower shines with sunset
Where peach and plum are blooming and the willow-cotton flies.
You have heard in your office the court-bell of twilight;
Birds find perches, officials head for home.
Your morning-jade will tinkle as you thread the golden palace;
You will bring the word of Heaven from the closing gates at night.
And I should serve there with you; but being full of years,
I have taken off official robes and am resting from my troubles.

poems.title: At Parting
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
I dismount from my horse and I offer you wine,
And I ask you where you are going and why.
And you answer: "I am discontent
And would rest at the foot of the southern mountain.
So give me leave and ask me no questions.
White clouds pass there without end."

poems.title: To Chi-wu Ch'ien Bound Home After Failing in an Examination
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
In a happy reign there should be no hermits;
The wise and able should consult together. . . .
So you, a man of the eastern mountains,
Gave up your life of picking herbs
And came all the way to the Gate of Gold —
But you found your devotion unavailing.
. . . To spend the Day of No Fire on one of the southern rivers,
You have mended your spring clothes here in these northern cities.
I pour you the farewell wine as you set out from the capital —
Soon I shall be left behind here by my bosom-friend.
In your sail-boat of sweet cinnamon-wood
You will float again toward your own thatch door,
Led along by distant trees
To a sunset shining on a far-away town.
. . . What though your purpose happened to fail,
Doubt not that some of us can hear high music.

poems.title: A Green Stream
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
I have sailed the River of Yellow Flowers,
Borne by the channel of a green stream,
Rounding ten thousand turns through the mountains
On a journey of less than thirty miles. . . .
Rapids hum over heaped rocks;
But where light grows dim in the thick pines,
The surface of an inlet sways with nut-horns
And weeds are lush along the banks.
. . . Down in my heart I have always been as pure
As this limpid water is. . . .
Oh, to remain on a broad flat rock
And to cast a fishing-line forever!

poems.title: A Farm-House on the Wei River
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
In the slant of the sun on the country-side,
Cattle and sheep trail home along the lane;
And a rugged old man in a thatch door
Leans on a staff and thinks of his son, the herd-boy.
There are whirring pheasants, full wheat-ears,
Silk-worms asleep, pared mulberry-leaves.
And the farmers, returning with hoes on their shoulders,
Hail one another familiarly.
. . . No wonder I long for the simple life
And am sighing the old song, Oh, to go Back Again!

poems.title: The Beautiful Hsi Shih
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Since beauty is honoured all over the Empire,
How could Hsi Shih remain humbly at home? —
Washing clothes at dawn by a southern lake —
And that evening a great lady in a palace of the north:
Lowly one day, no different from the others,
The next day exalted, everyone praising her.
No more would her own hands powder her face
Or arrange on her shoulders a silken robe.
And the more the King loved her, the lovelier she looked,
Blinding him away from wisdom.
. . . Girls who had once washed silk beside her
Were kept at a distance from her chariot.
And none of the girls in her neighbours' houses
By pursing their brows could copy her beauty.

poems.title: A Song of a Girl from Lo-yang
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
There's a girl from Lo-yang in the door across the street,
She looks fifteen, she may be a little older.
. . . While her master rides his rapid horse with jade bit and bridle,
Her handmaid brings her cod-fish in a golden plate.
On her painted pavilions, facing red towers,
Cornices are pink and green with peach-bloom and with willow.
Canopies of silk awn her seven-scented chair,
And rare fans shade her, home to her nine-flowered curtains.
Her lord, with rank and wealth and in the bud of life,
Exceeds in munificence the richest men of old.
He favours this girl of lowly birth, he has her taught to dance;
And he gives away his coral-trees to almost anyone.
The wind of dawn just stirs when his nine soft lights go out,
Those nine soft lights like petals in a flying chain of flowers.
Between dances she has barely time for singing over the songs;
No sooner is she dressed again than incense burns before her.
Those she knows in town are only the rich and the lavish,
And day and night she is visiting the hosts of the gayest mansions.
. . . Who notices the girl from Yueh with a face of white jade,
Humble, poor, alone, by the river, washing silk?

poems.title: A Song of an Old General
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
When he was a youth of fifteen or twenty,
He chased a wild horse, he caught him and rode him,
He shot the white-browed mountain tiger,
He defied the yellow-bristled Horseman of Yueh.
Fighting single-handed for a thousand miles,
With his naked dagger he could hold a multitude.
. . . Granted that the troops of China were as swift as heaven's thunder
And that Tartar soldiers perished in pitfalls fanged with iron,
General Wei Ch'ing's victory was only a thing of chance.
And General Li Kuang's thwarted effort was his fate, not his fault.
Since this man's retirement he is looking old and worn:
Experience of the world has hastened his white hairs.
Though once his quick dart never missed the right eye of a bird,
Now knotted veins and tendons make his left arm like an osier.
He is sometimes at the road-side selling melons from his garden,
He is sometimes planting willows round his hermitage.
His lonely lane is shut away by a dense grove,
His vacant window looks upon the far cold mountains. . . .
But, if he prayed, the waters would come gushing for his men
And never would he wanton his cause away with wine.
. . . War-clouds are spreading, under the Ho-lan Range;
Back and forth, day and night, go feathered messages;
In the three River Provinces, the governors call young men —
And five imperial edicts have summoned the old general.
So he dusts his iron coat and shines it like snow —
Waves his dagger from its jade hilt in a dance of starry steel.
He is ready with his strong northern bow to smite the Tartar chieftain —
That never a foreign war-dress may affront the Emperor.
. . . There once was an aged Prefect, forgotten and far away,
Who still could manage triumph with a single stroke.

poems.title: A Song of Peach-Blossom River
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
A fisherman is drifting, enjoying the spring mountains,
And the peach-trees on both banks lead him to an ancient source.
Watching the fresh-coloured trees, he never thinks of distance
Till he comes to the end of the blue stream and suddenly — strange men!
It's a cave — with a mouth so narrow that he has to crawl through;
But then it opens wide again on a broad and level path —
And far beyond he faces clouds crowning a reach of trees,
And thousands of houses shadowed round with flowers and bamboos. . . .
Woodsmen tell him their names in the ancient speech of Han;
And clothes of the Ch'in Dynasty are worn by all these people
Living on the uplands, above the Wu-ling River,
On farms and in gardens that are like a world apart,
Their dwellings at peace under pines in the clear moon,
Until sunrise fills the low sky with crowing and barking.
. . . At news of a stranger the people all assemble,
And each of them invites him home and asks him where he was born.
Alleys and paths are cleared for him of petals in the morning,
And fishermen and farmers bring him their loads at dusk. . . .
They had left the world long ago, they had come here seeking refuge;
They have lived like angels ever since, blessedly far away,
No one in the cave knowing anything outside,
Outsiders viewing only empty mountains and thick clouds.
. . . The fisherman, unaware of his great good fortune,
Begins to think of country, of home, of worldly ties,
Finds his way out of the cave again, past mountains and past rivers,
Intending some time to return, when he has told his kin.
He studies every step he takes, fixes it well in mind,
And forgets that cliffs and peaks may vary their appearance.
. . . It is certain that to enter through the deepness of the mountain,
A green river leads you, into a misty wood.
But now, with spring-floods everywhere and floating peach-petals —
Which is the way to go, to find that hidden source?

poems.title: 送朱大入秦 (Song zhu da ru qin)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
避人五陵去，寶劍值千金。
分手脫相贈，平生一片心。

poems.title: 相思 (Xiang si)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
紅豆生南國，春來發幾枝。
願君多采擷，此物最相思。

poems.title: 雜詩三首·其二 (Za shi san shou, qi er)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
君自故鄉來，應知故鄉事。
來日綺窗前，寒梅著花未？

poems.title: 鹿柴 (Lu chai)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
空山不見人，但聞人語響。
返景入深林，復照青苔上。

poems.title: 竹裏館 (Zhu li guan)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
獨坐幽篁裏，彈琴復長嘯。
深林人不知，明月來相照。

poems.title: 山中送別 (Shan zhong song bie)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.note: 五言絕句. Also titled 送別.
poems.text:
山中相送罷，日暮掩柴扉。
春草明年綠，王孫歸不歸？

poems.title: 九月九日憶山東兄弟 (Jiu yue jiu ri yi shan dong xiong di)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
獨在異鄉爲異客，每逢佳節倍思親。
遙知兄弟登高處，遍插茱萸少一人。

poems.title: 送梓州李使君 (Song zi zhou li shi jun)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
萬壑樹參天，千山響杜鵑。
山中一夜雨，樹杪百重泉。
漢女輸橦布，巴人訟芋田。
文翁翻教授，不敢倚先賢。

poems.title: 漢江臨泛 (Han jiang lin fan)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.note: 五言律詩. Also titled 漢江臨眺.
poems.text:
楚塞三湘接，荊門九派通。
江流天地外，山色有無中。
郡邑浮前浦，波瀾動遠空。
襄陽好風日，留醉與山翁。

poems.title: 終南別業 (Zhong nan bie ye)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
中歲頗好道，晚家南山陲。
興來每獨往，勝事空自知。
行到水窮處，坐看雲起時。
偶然值林叟，談笑無還期。

poems.title: 終南山 (Zhong nan shan)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
太乙近天都，連山接海隅。
白雲回望合，青靄入看無。
分野中峯變，陰晴衆壑殊。
欲投人處宿，隔水問樵夫。

poems.title: 酬張少府 (Chou zhang shao fu)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
晚年唯好靜，萬事不關心。
自顧無長策，空知返舊林。
松風吹解帶，山月照彈琴。
君問窮通理，漁歌入浦深。

poems.title: 過香積寺 (Guo xiang ji si)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
不知香積寺，數裏入雲峯。
古木無人徑，深山何處鐘。
泉聲咽危石，日色冷青松。
薄暮空潭曲，安禪製毒龍。

poems.title: 輞川閒居贈裴秀才迪 (Wang chuan xian ju zeng pei xiu cai di)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
寒山轉蒼翠，秋水日潺湲。
倚杖柴門外，臨風聽暮蟬。
渡頭餘落日，墟里上孤煙。
復值接輿醉，狂歌五柳前。

poems.title: 山居秋暝 (Shan ju qiu ming)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
空山新雨後，天氣晚來秋。
明月鬆間照，清泉石上流。
竹喧歸浣女，蓮動下漁舟。
隨意春芳歇，王孫自可留。

poems.title: 歸嵩山作 (Gui song shan zuo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
清川帶長薄，車馬去閒閒。
流水如有意，暮禽相與還。
荒城臨古渡，落日滿秋山。
迢遞嵩高下，歸來且閉關。

poems.title: 酬郭給事 (Chou guo ji shi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
洞門高閣靄餘輝，桃李陰陰柳絮飛。
禁裏疏鍾官舍晚，省中啼鳥吏人稀。
晨搖玉佩趨金殿，夕奉天書拜瑣闈。
強欲從君無那老，將因臥病解朝衣。

poems.title: 和賈舍人早朝大明宮之作 (He jia she ren zao chao da ming gong zhi zuo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
絳幘雞人送曉籌，尚衣方進翠雲裘。
九天閶闔開宮殿，萬國衣冠拜冕旒。
日色才臨仙掌動，香菸欲傍袞龍浮。
朝罷須裁五色詔，佩聲歸向鳳池頭。

poems.title: 奉和聖制從蓬萊向興慶閣道中留春雨中春望之作應制 (Feng he sheng zhi cong peng lai xiang xing qing ge dao zhong liu chun yu zhong chun wang zhi zuo ying zhi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
渭水自縈秦塞曲，黃山舊繞漢宮斜。
鑾輿迥出千門柳，閣道回看上苑花。
雲裏帝城雙鳳闕，雨中春樹萬人家。
爲乘陽氣行時令，不是宸遊玩物華。

poems.title: 積雨輞川莊作 (Ji yu wang chuan zhuang zuo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.note: 七言律詩. Also titled 秋歸輞川莊作.
poems.text:
積雨空林煙火遲，蒸藜炊黍餉東菑。
漠漠水田飛白鷺，陰陰夏木囀黃鸝。
山中習靜觀朝槿，松下清齋折露葵。
野老與人爭席罷，海鷗何事更相疑。

poems.title: 渭川田家 (Wei chuan tian jia)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
斜陽照墟落，窮巷牛羊歸。
野老念牧童，倚杖候荊扉。
雉雊麥苗秀，蠶眠桑葉稀。
田夫荷鋤至，相見語依依。
即此羨閒逸，悵然吟式微。

poems.title: 西施詠 (Xi shi yong)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
豔色天下重，西施寧久微。
朝爲越溪女，暮作吳宮妃。
賤日豈殊衆，貴來方悟稀。
邀人傅香粉，不自著羅衣。
君寵益嬌態，君憐無是非。
當時浣紗伴，莫得同車歸。
持謝鄰家子，效顰安可希。

poems.title: 送別 (Song bie)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
下馬飲君酒，問君何所之？
君言不得意，歸臥南山陲。
但去莫復問，白雲無盡時。

poems.title: 送綦毋潛落第還鄉 (Song qi wu qian luo di huan xiang)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
聖代無隱者，英靈盡來歸。
遂令東山客，不得顧采薇。
既至金門遠，孰雲吾道非。
江淮度寒食，京洛縫春衣。
置酒長安道，同心與我違。
行當浮桂棹，未幾拂荊扉。
遠樹帶行客，孤城當落暉。
吾謀適不用，勿謂知音稀。

poems.title: 青溪 (Qing xi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.note: 五言古詩. Also titled 過青溪水作.
poems.text:
言入黃花川，每逐清溪水。
隨山將萬轉，趣途無百里。
聲喧亂石中，色靜深鬆裏。
漾漾泛菱荇，澄澄映葭葦。
我心素已閒，清川澹如此。
請留磐石上，垂釣將已矣。

poems.title: 送元二使安西 (Song yuan er shi an xi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.note: 樂府. Also titled 渭城曲.
poems.text:
渭城朝雨浥輕塵，客舍青青柳色新。
勸君更盡一杯酒，西出陽關無故人。

poems.title: 秋夜曲 (Qiu ye qu)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
桂魄初生秋露微，輕羅已薄未更衣。
銀箏夜久殷勤弄，心怯空房不忍歸。

poems.title: 洛陽女兒行 (Luo yang nü er xing)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
洛陽女兒對門居，纔可顏容十五餘。
良人玉勒乘驄馬，侍女金盤膾鯉魚。
畫閣朱樓盡相望，紅桃綠柳垂檐向。
羅帷送上七香車，寶扇迎歸九華帳。
狂夫富貴在青春，意氣驕奢劇季倫。
自憐碧玉親教舞，不惜珊瑚持與人。
春窗曙滅九微火，九微片片飛花瑣。
戲罷曾無理曲時，妝成祗是薰香坐。
城中相識盡繁華，日夜經過趙李家。
誰憐越女顏如玉，貧賤江頭自浣紗。

poems.title: 老將行 (Lao jiang xing)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
少年十五二十時，步行奪得胡馬騎。
射殺山中白額虎，肯數鄴下黃鬚兒！
一身轉戰三千里，一劍曾當百萬師。
漢兵奮迅如霹靂，虜騎崩騰畏蒺藜。
衛青不敗由天幸，李廣無功緣數奇。
自從棄置便衰朽，世事蹉跎成白首。
昔時飛箭無全目，今日垂楊生左肘。
路旁時賣故侯瓜，門前學種先生柳。
蒼茫古木連窮巷，寥落寒山對虛牖。
誓令疏勒出飛泉，不似潁川空使酒。
賀蘭山下陣如雲，羽檄交馳日夕聞。
節使三河募年少，詔書五道出將軍。
試拂鐵衣如雪色，聊持寶劍動星文。
願得燕弓射大將，恥令越甲鳴吾君。
莫嫌舊日雲中守，猶堪一戰取功勳。

poems.title: 桃源行 (Tao yuan xing)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
漁舟逐水愛山春，兩岸桃花夾古津。
坐看紅樹不知遠，行盡青溪不見人。
山口潛行始隈隩，山開曠望旋平陸。
遙看一處攢雲樹，近入千家散花竹。
樵客初傳漢姓名，居人未改秦衣服。
居人共住武陵源，還從物外起田園。
月明松下房櫳靜，日出雲中雞犬喧。
驚聞俗客爭來集，競引還家問都邑。
平明閭巷掃花開，薄暮漁樵乘水入。
初因避地去人間，及至成仙遂不還。
峽裏誰知有人事，世中遙望空雲山。
不疑靈境難聞見，塵心未盡思鄉縣。
出洞無論隔山水，辭家終擬長遊衍。
自謂經過舊不迷，安知峯壑今來變。
當時只記入山深，青溪幾度到雲林。
春來遍是桃花水，不辨仙源何處尋。

poems.title: 早春行 (Zao chun xing)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
紫梅發初遍，黃鳥歌猶澁。
誰家折楊女，弄春如不及。
愛水看妝坐，羞人映花立。
香畏風吹散，衣愁露霑濕。
玉閨青門裏，日落香車入。
游衍益相思，含啼向綵帷。
憶君長入夢，歸晚更生疑。
不及紅簷燕，雙棲綠草時。

poems.title: 贈祖三詠 (Zeng zu san yong)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
蟏蛸挂虛牖，蟋蟀鳴前除。
歲晏涼風至，君子復何如。
高館闃無人，離居不可道。
閑門寂已閉，落日照秋草。
雖有近音信，千里阻河關。
中復客汝潁，去年歸舊山。
結交二十載，不得一日展。
貧病子既深，契闊余不淺。
仲秋雖未歸，暮秋以爲期。
良會詎幾日，終日長相思。

poems.title: 戲贈張五弟諲三首·其一 (Xi zeng zhang wu di yin san shou, qi yi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
吾弟東山時，心尚一何遠。
日高猶自臥，鐘動始能飯。
領上髪未梳，牀頭書不卷。
清川興悠悠，空林對偃蹇。
青苔石上淨，細草松下軟。
窗外鳥聲閑，階前虎心善。
徒然萬象多，澹爾太虛緬。
一知與物平，自顧爲人淺。
對君忽自得，浮念不煩遣。

poems.title: 戲贈張五弟諲三首·其二 (Xi zeng zhang wu di yin san shou, qi er)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
張弟五車書，讀書仍隱居。
染翰過草聖，賦詩輕子虛。
閉門二室下，隱居十年餘。
宛是野人野，時從漁夫漁。
秋風自蕭索，五柳高且疎。
望此去人世，渡水向吾廬。
歲晏同攜手，只應君與予。

poems.title: 贈裴十迪 (Zeng pei shi di)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
風景日夕佳，與君賦新詩。
澹然望遠空，如意方支頤。
春風動百草，蘭蕙生我籬。
曖曖日暖閨，田家來致詞。
欣欣春還臯，淡淡水生陂。
桃李雖未開，荑萼滿芳枝。
請君理還策，敢告將農時。

poems.title: 奉寄韋太守陟 (Feng ji wei tai shou zhi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
荒城自蕭索，萬里山河空。
天高秋日逈，嘹唳聞歸鴻。
寒塘映衰草，高館落疎桐。
臨此歲方晏，顧景詠悲翁。
故人不可見，寂寞平陵東。

poems.title: 和使君五郎西樓望遠思歸 (He shi jun wu lang xi lou wang yuan si gui)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
高樓望所思，目極情未畢。
枕上見千里，窗中窺萬室。
悠悠長路人，曖曖遠郊日。
惆悵極浦外，迢遞孤煙出。
能賦屬上才，思歸同下秩。
故鄉不可見，雲水空如一。

poems.title: 酬黎居士淅川作 (Chou li ju shi xi chuan zuo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
儂家真箇去，公定隨儂否。
著處是蓮花，無心變楊柳。
松龕藏藥裹，石脣安茶臼。
氣味當共知，那能不攜手。

poems.title: 送宇文太守赴宣城 (Song yu wen tai shou fu xuan cheng)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
寥落雲外山，迢遞舟中賞。
鐃吹發西江，秋空多清響。
地迥古城蕪，月明寒潮廣。
時賽敬亭神，復解罟師網。
何處寄相思？南風吹五兩。

poems.title: 齊州送祖三 (Qi zhou song zu san)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
相逢方一笑，相送還成泣。
祖帳已傷離，荒城復愁入。
天寒遠山淨，日暮長河急。
解纜君已遙，望君猶佇立。

poems.title: 觀別者 (Guan bie zhe)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
青青楊柳陌，陌上別離人。
愛子遊燕趙，高堂有老親。
不行無可養，行去百憂新。
切切委兄弟，依依向四鄰。
都門帳飲畢，從此謝親賓。
揮涕逐前侶，含悽動征輪。
車徒望不見，時見起行塵。
吾亦辭家久，看之淚滿巾。

poems.title: 別弟縉後登青龍寺望藍田山 (Bie di jin hou deng qing long si wang lan tian shan)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
陌上新離別，蒼茫四郊晦。
登高不見君，故山復雲外。
遠樹蔽行人，長天隱秋塞。
心悲宦遊子，何處飛征蓋。

poems.title: 冬日遊覽 (Dong ri you lan)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
步出城東門，試騁千里目。
青山橫蒼林，赤日團平陸。
渭北走邯鄲，關東出函谷。
秦地萬方會，來朝九州牧。
雞鳴咸陽中，冠蓋相追逐。
丞相過列侯，羣公餞光祿。
相如方老病，獨歸茂陵宿。

poems.title: 藍田山石門精舍 (Lan tian shan shi men jing she)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
落日山水好，漾舟信歸風。
探奇不覺遠，因以緣源窮。
遙愛雲木秀，初疑路不同。
安知清流轉，偶與前山通。
捨舟理輕策，果然愜所適。
老僧四五人，逍遙蔭松栢。
朝梵林未曙，夜禪山更寂。
道心及牧童，世事問樵客。
暝宿長林下，焚香臥瑤席。
澗芳襲人衣，山月暎石壁。
再尋畏迷誤，明發更登歷。
笑謝桃源人，花紅復來覿。

poems.title: 崔濮陽兄季重前山興 (Cui pu yang xiong ji zhong qian shan xing)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
秋色有佳興，況君池上閑。
悠悠西林下，自識門前山。
千里橫黛色，數峰出雲間。
嵯峨對秦國，合沓藏荆關。
殘雨斜日照，夕嵐飛鳥還。
故人今尚爾，歎息此頹顏。

poems.title: 春中田園作 (Chun zhong tian yuan zuo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
屋上春鳩鳴，村邊杏花白。
持斧伐遠揚，荷鋤覘泉脈。
歸燕識故巢，舊人看新曆。
臨觴忽不御，惆悵遠行客。

poems.title: 過李楫宅 (Guo li ji zhai)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
閑門秋草色，終日無車馬。
客來深巷中，犬吠寒林下。
散髪時未簪，道書行尚把。
與我同心人，樂道安貧者。
一罷宜城酌，還歸洛陽社。

poems.title: 飯覆釜山僧 (Fan fu fu shan seng)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
晚知清淨理，日與人羣疎。
將候遠山僧，先期埽弊廬。
果從雲峰裏，顧我蓬蒿居。
藉草飯松屑，焚香看道書。
然燈晝欲盡，鳴磬夜方初。
一悟寂爲樂，此日閑有餘。
思歸何必深，身世猶空虛。

poems.title: 瓜園詩 (Gua yuan shi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
余適欲鋤瓜，倚鋤聽叩門。
鳴騶導驄馬，常從夾朱軒。
窮巷正傳呼，故人儻相存。
攜手追涼風，放心望乾坤。
藹藹帝王州，宮觀一何繁。
林端出綺道，殿頂搖華幡。
素懷在青山，若值白雲屯。
回風城西雨，返景原上村。
前酌盈尊酒，往往聞清言。
黃鸝囀深木，朱槿照中園。
猶羨松下客，石上聞清猿。

poems.title: 自大散以往深林密竹磴道盤曲四五十里至黃牛嶺見黃花川 (Zi da san yi wang shen lin mi zhu deng dao pan qu si wu shi li zhi huang niu ling jian huang hua chuan)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
危徑幾萬轉，數里將三休。
回環見徒侶，隱暎隔林丘。
颯颯松上雨，潺潺石中流。
靜言深谿裏，長嘯高山頭。
望見南山陽，白露靄悠悠。
青臯麗已淨，綠樹鬱如浮。
曾是厭蒙密，曠然銷人憂。

poems.title: 宿鄭州 (Su zheng zhou)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
朝與周人辭，暮投鄭人宿。
他鄉絕儔侶，孤客親僮僕。
宛洛望不見，秋霖晦平陸。
田父草際歸，村童雨中牧。
主人東臯上，時稼遶茅屋。
蟲思機杼悲，雀喧禾黍熟。
明當渡京水，昨晚猶金谷。
此去欲何言，窮邊狥微祿。

poems.title: 苦熱 (Ku re)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
赤日滿天地，火雲成山嶽。
草木盡焦卷，川澤皆竭涸。
輕紈覺衣重，密樹苦陰薄。
莞簟不可近，絺綌再三濯。
思出宇宙外，曠然在寥廓。
長風萬里來，江海蕩煩濁。
却顧身爲患，始知心未覺。
忽入甘露門，宛然清涼樂。

poems.title: 納涼 (Na liang)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
喬木萬餘株，清流貫其中。
前臨大川口，豁達來長風。
漣漪涵白沙，素鮪如遊空。
偃臥盤石上，翻濤沃微躬。
漱流復濯足，前對釣魚翁。
貪餌凡幾許，徒思蓮葉東。

poems.title: 羽林騎閨人 (Yu lin qi gui ren)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
秋月臨高城，城中管弦思。
離人堂上愁，稚子階前戲。
出門復暎戶，望望青絲騎。
行人過欲盡，狂夫終不至。
左右寂無言，相看共垂淚。

poems.title: 偶然作六首·其一 (Ou ran zuo liu shou, qi yi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
楚國有狂夫，茫然無心想。
散髪不冠帶，行歌南陌上。
孔丘與之言，仁義莫能獎。
未嘗肯問天，何事須擊壤。
復笑采薇人，胡爲乃長往。

poems.title: 偶然作六首·其二 (Ou ran zuo liu shou, qi er)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
田舍有老翁，垂白衡門裏。
有時農事閑，斗酒呼鄰里。
喧聒茅簷下，或坐或復起。
短褐不爲薄，園葵固足美。
動則長子孫，不曾向城市。
五帝與三王，古來稱天子。
干戈將揖讓，畢竟何者是。
得意苟爲樂，野田安足鄙。
且當放懷去，行行沒餘齒。

poems.title: 偶然作六首·其三 (Ou ran zuo liu shou, qi san)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
日夕見太行，沈吟未能去。
問君何以然，世網嬰我故。
小妹日成長，兄弟未有娶。
家貧祿既薄，儲蓄非有素。
幾回欲奮飛，踟躕復相顧。
孫登長嘯臺，松竹有遺處。
相去詎幾許，故人在中路。
愛染日已薄，禪寂日已固。
忽乎吾將行，寧俟歲云暮。

poems.title: 偶然作六首·其四 (Ou ran zuo liu shou, qi si)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
陶潛任天真，其性頗躭酒。
自從棄官來，家貧不能有。
九月九日時，菊花空滿手。
中心竊自思，儻有人送否。
白衣攜壺觴，果來遺老叟。
且喜得斟酌，安問升與斗。
奮衣野田中，今日嗟無負。
兀傲迷東西，蓑笠不能守。
傾倒強行行，酣歌歸五柳。
生事不曾問，肯媿家中婦。

poems.title: 偶然作六首·其五 (Ou ran zuo liu shou, qi wu)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
趙女彈箜篌，復能邯鄲舞。
夫壻輕薄兒，鬬雞事齊主。
黃金買歌笑，用錢不復數。
許史相經過，高門盈四牡。
客舍有儒生，昂藏出鄒魯。
讀書三十年，腰間無尺組。
被服聖人教，一生自窮苦。

poems.title: 偶然作六首·其六 (Ou ran zuo liu shou, qi liu)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
老來懶賦詩，惟有老相隨。
宿世謬詞客，前身應畫師。
不能捨餘習，偶被世人知。
名字本皆是，此心還不知。

poems.title: 哭殷遙 (Ku yin yao)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
人生能幾何，畢竟歸無形。
念君等爲死，萬事傷人情。
慈母未及葬，一女纔十齡。
泱漭寒郊外，蕭條聞哭聲。
浮雲爲蒼茫，飛鳥不能鳴。
行人何寂寞，白日自淒清。
憶昔君在時，問我學無生。
勸君苦不早，令君無所成。
故人各有贈，又不及生平。
負爾非一途，慟哭返柴荆。

poems.title: 夷門歌 (Yi men ge)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
七雄雄雌猶未分，攻城殺將何紛紛。
秦兵益圍邯鄲急，魏王不救平原君。
公子爲嬴停駟馬，執轡愈恭意愈下。
亥爲屠肆鼓刀人，嬴乃夷門抱關者。
非但慷慨獻良謀，意氣兼將身命酬。
向風刎頸送公子，七十老翁何所求。

poems.title: 隴頭吟 (Long tou yin)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
長安少年遊俠客，夜上戍樓看太白。
隴頭明月迥臨關，隴上行人夜吹笛。
關西老將不勝愁，駐馬聽之雙淚流。
身經大小百餘戰，麾下偏裨萬戶侯。
蘇武纔爲典屬國，節旄空盡海西頭。

poems.title: 燕支行 (Yan zhi xing)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
漢家天將才且雄，來時謁帝明光宮。
萬乘親推雙闕下，千官出餞五陵東。
誓辭甲第金門裏，身作長城玉塞中。
衞霍才堪一騎將，朝廷不數貳師功。
趙魏燕韓多勁卒，關西俠少何咆勃。
報讐只是聞嘗膽，飲酒不曾妨刮骨。
畫戟雕戈白日寒，連旗大斾黃塵沒。
疊鼓遙翻瀚海波，鳴笳亂動天山月。
麒麟錦帶佩吳鉤，颯沓青驪躍紫騮。
拔劒已斷天驕臂，歸鞍共飲月支頭。
漢兵大呼一當百，虜騎相看哭且愁。
教戰雖令赴湯火，終知上將先伐謀。

poems.title: 同崔傅答賢弟 (Tong cui fu da xian di)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
洛陽才子姑蘇客，桂苑殊非故鄉陌。
九江楓樹幾回青，一片揚州五湖白。
揚州時有下江兵，蘭陵鎮前吹笛聲。
夜火人歸富春郭，秋風鶴唳石頭城。
周郎陸弟爲儔侶，對舞前溪歌白紵。
曲几書留小史家，草堂棋賭山陰墅。
衣冠若話外臺臣，先數夫君席上珍。
更聞臺閣求三語，遙想風流第一人。

poems.title: 故人張諲工詩善易卜兼能丹青草隸頃以詩見贈聊獲酬之 (Gu ren zhang yin gong shi shan yi bo jian neng dan qing cao li qing yi shi jian zeng liao huo chou zhi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
不逐城東遊俠兒，隱囊紗帽坐彈棋。
蜀中夫子時開卦，洛下書生解詠詩。
藥闌花逕衡門裏，時復據梧聊隱几。
屏風誤點惑孫郎，團扇草書輕內史。
故園高枕度三春，永日垂帷絕四鄰。
自想蔡邕今已老，更將書籍使何人。

poems.title: 送崔五太守 (Song cui wu tai shou)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
長安廄吏來到門，朱文露網動行軒。
黃花縣西九折坂，玉樹宮南五丈原。
襃斜谷中不容幰，唯有白雲當露冕。
子午山裏杜鵑啼，嘉陵水頭行客飯。
劒門忽斷蜀川開，萬井雙流滿眼來。
霧中遠樹刀州出，天際澄江巴字回。
使君年紀三十餘，少年白皙專城居。
欲持畫省郎官筆，回與臨邛父老書。

poems.title: 寒食城東即事 (Han shi cheng dong ji shi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
清溪一道穿桃李，演漾綠蒲涵白芷。
溪上人家凡幾家，落花半落東流水。
蹴鞠屢過飛鳥上，鞦韆競出垂楊裏。
少年分日作遨遊，不用清明兼上巳。

poems.title: 黃雀癡 (Huang que chi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
黃雀癡，黃雀癡，謂言青鷇是我兒。
一一口銜食，養得成毛衣。
到大啁啾解游颺，各自東西南北飛。
薄暮空巢上，羇雌獨自歸。
鳳凰九雛亦如此，慎莫愁思顦顇損容輝。

poems.title: 荅張五弟 (Da zhang wu di)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
終南有茅屋，前對終南山。
終年無客常閉關，終日無心長自閑。
不妨飲酒復垂釣，君但能來相往還。

poems.title: 送友人歸山歌二首·其一 (Song you ren gui shan ge er shou, qi yi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
山寂寂兮無人，又蒼蒼兮多木。
羣龍兮滿朝，君何爲兮空谷。
文寡和兮思深，道難知兮行獨。
悅石上兮流泉，與松間兮草屋。
入雲中兮養雞，上山頭兮抱犢。
神與棗兮如瓜，虎賣杏兮收穀。
愧不才兮妨賢，嫌既老兮貪祿。
誓解印兮相從，何詹尹兮何卜。

poems.title: 送友人歸山歌二首·其二 (Song you ren gui shan ge er shou, qi er)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
山中人兮欲歸，雲冥冥兮雨霏霏，水驚波兮翠菅靡。
白鷺忽兮翻飛，君不可兮褰衣。
山萬重兮一雲，混天地兮不分。
樹晻曖兮氛氳，猿不見兮空聞。
忽山西兮夕陽，見東臯兮遠村。
平蕪綠兮千里，眇惆悵兮思君。

poems.title: 魚山神女祠歌·迎神 (Yu shan shen nü ci ge, ying shen)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
坎坎擊鼓，魚山之下。
吹洞簫，望極浦，女巫進，紛屢舞。
陳瑤席，湛清酤，風淒淒兮夜雨。
不知神之來兮不來，使我心兮苦復苦。

poems.title: 從岐王過楊氏別業應教 (Cong qi wang guo yang shi bie ye ying jiao)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
楊子談經所，淮王載酒過。
興闌啼鳥換，坐久落花多。
逕轉廻銀燭，林開散玉珂。
嚴城時未啓，前路擁笙歌。

poems.title: 早朝 (Zao chao)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
柳暗百花明，春深五鳳城。
城烏睥睨曉，宮井轆轤聲。
方朔金門侍，班姬玉輦迎。
仍聞遣方士，東海訪蓬瀛。

poems.title: 同崔員外秋宵寓直 (Tong cui yuan wai qiu xiao yu zhi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
建禮高秋夜，承明候曉過。
九門寒漏徹，萬井曙鐘多。
月迥藏珠斗，雲消出絳河。
更慙衰朽質，南陌共鳴珂。

poems.title: 寄荆州張丞相 (Ji jing zhou zhang cheng xiang)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
所思竟何在，悵望深荆門。
舉世無相識，終身思舊恩。
方將與農圃，藝植老丘園。
目盡南飛鴈，何由寄一言。

poems.title: 和尹諫議史館山池 (He yin jian yi shi guan shan chi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
雲館接天居，霓裳侍玉除。
春池百子外，芳樹萬年餘。
洞有仙人籙，山藏太史書。
君恩深漢帝，且莫上空虛。

poems.title: 奉和楊駙馬六郎秋夜即事 (Feng he yang fu ma liu lang qiu ye ji shi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
高樓月似霜，秋夜鬱金堂。
對坐彈盧女，同看舞鳳凰。
少兒多送酒，小玉更焚香。
結束平陽騎，明朝入建章。

poems.title: 酬虞部蘇員外過藍田別業不見留之作 (Chou yu bu su yuan wai guo lan tian bie ye bu jian liu zhi zuo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
貧居依谷口，喬木帶荒村。
石路枉廻駕，山家誰候門。
漁舟膠凍浦，獵火燒寒原。
唯有白雲外，疎鐘聞夜猿。

poems.title: 送丘爲落第歸江東 (Song qiu wei luo di gui jiang dong)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
憐君不得意，況復柳條春。
爲客黃金盡，還家白髮新。
五湖三畝宅，萬里一歸人。
知爾不能薦，羞稱獻納臣。

poems.title: 送岐州源長史歸 (Song qi zhou yuan zhang shi gui)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
握手一相送，心悲安可論。
秋風正蕭索，客散孟嘗門。
故驛通槐里，長亭下槿原。
征西舊旌節，從此向河源。

poems.title: 送張道士歸山 (Song zhang dao shi gui shan)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
先生何處去，王屋訪茅君。
別婦留丹訣，驅雞入白雲。
人間若剩住，天上復離羣。
當作遼城鶴，仙歌使爾聞。

poems.title: 送平澹然判官 (Song ping dan ran pan guan)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
不識陽關路，新從定遠侯。
黃雲斷春色，畫角起邊愁。
瀚海經年到，交河出塞流。
須令外國使，知飲月氏頭。

poems.title: 送劉司直赴安西 (Song liu si zhi fu an xi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
絕域陽關道，胡沙與塞塵。
三春時有雁，萬里少行人。
苜蓿隨天馬，葡萄逐漢臣。
當令外國懼，不敢覓和親。

poems.title: 送張五諲歸宣城 (Song zhang wu yin gui xuan cheng)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
五湖千萬里，況復五湖西。
漁浦南陵郭，人家春穀谿。
欲歸江淼淼，未到草萋萋。
憶想蘭陵鎮，可宜猿更啼。

poems.title: 送楊長史赴果州 (Song yang zhang shi fu guo zhou)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
襃斜不容幰，之子去何之。
鳥道一千里，猿聲十二時。
官橋祭酒客，山木女郎祠。
別後同明月，君應聽子規。

poems.title: 送邢桂州 (Song xing gui zhou)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
鐃吹喧京口，風波下洞庭。
赭圻將赤岸，擊汰復揚舲。
日落江湖白，潮來天地青。
明珠歸合浦，應逐使臣星。

poems.title: 送孟六歸襄陽 (Song meng liu gui xiang yang)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
杜門不復出，久與世情疎。
以此爲良策，勸君歸舊廬。
醉歌田舍酒，笑讀古人書。
好是一生事，無勞獻子虛。

poems.title: 初出濟州別城中故人 (Chu chu ji zhou bie cheng zhong gu ren)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
微官易得罪，謫去濟川陰。
執政方持法，明君照此心。
閭閻河潤上，井邑海雲深。
縱有歸來日，各愁年鬢侵。

poems.title: 登裴秀才迪小臺 (Deng pei xiu cai di xiao tai)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
端居不出戶，滿目望雲山。
落日鳥邊下，秋原人外閑。
遙知遠林際，不見此簷間。
好客多乘月，應門莫上關。

poems.title: 遊李山人所居因題屋壁 (You li shan ren suo ju yin ti wu bi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
世上皆如夢，狂來止自歌。
問年松樹老，有地竹林多。
藥倩韓康賣，門容尚子過。
翻嫌枕席上，無那白雲何。

poems.title: 過崔駙馬山池 (Guo cui fu ma shan chi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
畫樓吹笛妓，金椀酒家胡。
錦石稱貞女，青松學大夫。
脫貂貰桂醑，射雁與山廚。
聞道高陽會，愚公谷正愚。

poems.title: 濟上四賢詠·成文學 (Ji shang si xian yong, cheng wen xue)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
寶劒千金裝，登君白玉堂。
身爲平原客，家有邯鄲娼。
使氣公卿坐，論心遊俠場。
中年不得意，謝病客遊梁。

poems.title: 過福禪師蘭若 (Guo fu chan shi lan ruo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
巖壑轉微逕，雲林隱法堂。
羽人飛奏樂，天女跪焚香。
竹外峰偏曙，藤陰水更涼。
欲知禪坐久，行路長春芳。

poems.title: 登辨覺寺 (Deng bian jue si)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
竹徑從初地，蓮峰出化城。
窗中三楚盡，林上九江平。
軟草承趺坐，長松響梵聲。
空居法雲外，觀世得無生。

poems.title: 晚春嚴少尹與諸公見過 (Wan chun yan shao yin yu zhu gong jian guo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
松菊荒三逕，圖書共五車。
烹葵邀上客，看竹到貧家。
鵲乳先春草，鶯啼過落花。
自憐黃髪暮，一倍惜年華。

poems.title: 歸輞川作 (Gui wang chuan zuo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
谷口疎鐘動，漁樵稍欲稀。
悠然遠山暮，獨向白雲歸。
菱蔓弱難定，楊花輕易飛。
東臯春草色，惆悵掩柴扉。

poems.title: 山居即事 (Shan ju ji shi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
寂寞掩柴扉，蒼茫對落暉。
鶴巢松樹遍，人訪蓽門稀。
綠竹含新粉，紅蓮落故衣。
渡頭煙火起，處處采菱歸。

poems.title: 輞川閑居 (Wang chuan xian ju)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
一從歸白社，不復到青門。
時倚檐前樹，遠看原上村。
青菰臨水拔，白鳥向山翻。
寂寞於陵子，桔槔方灌園。

poems.title: 涼州郊外遊望 (Liang zhou jiao wai you wang)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
野老纔三戶，邊村少四鄰。
婆娑依里社，簫鼓賽田神。
灑酒澆芻狗，焚香拜木人。
女巫紛屢舞，羅襪自生塵。

poems.title: 觀獵 (Guan lie)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
風勁角弓鳴，將軍獵渭城。
草枯鷹眼疾，雪盡馬蹄輕。
忽過新豐市，還歸細柳營。
迴看射鵰處，千里暮雲平。

poems.title: 汎前陂 (Fan qian bei)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
秋空自明迥，況復遠人間。
暢以沙際鶴，兼之雲外山。
澄波澹將夕，清月皓方閑。
此夜任孤櫂，夷猶殊未還。

poems.title: 使至塞上 (Shi zhi sai shang)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
單車欲問邊，屬國過居延。
征蓬出漢塞，歸雁入胡天。
大漠孤煙直，長河落日圓。
蕭關逢候吏，都護在燕然。

poems.title: 戲題示蕭氏甥 (Xi ti shi xiao shi sheng)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
憐爾解臨池，渠爺未學詩。
老夫何足似，弊宅倘因之。
蘆筍穿荷葉，菱花罥雁兒。
郗公不易勝，莫著外家欺。

poems.title: 晚春歸思 (Wan chun gui si)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
新妝可憐色，落日卷羅帷。
鑪氣清珍簟，牆陰上玉墀。
春蟲飛網戶，暮雀隱花枝。
向晚多愁思，閑窗桃李時。

poems.title: 秋夜獨坐 (Qiu ye du zuo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
獨坐悲雙鬢，空堂欲二更。
雨中山果落，燈下草蟲鳴。
白髮終難變，黃金不可成。
欲知除老病，唯有學無生。

poems.title: 奉和聖製上巳於望春亭觀禊飲應制 (Feng he sheng zhi shang si yu wang chun ting guan xi yin ying zhi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
長樂青門外，宜春小苑東。
樓開萬井上，輦過百花中。
畫鷁移仙妓，金貂列上公。
清歌邀落日，妙舞向春風。
渭水明秦甸，黃山入漢宮。
君王來祓禊，灞滻亦朝宗。

poems.title: 奉和聖製暮春送朝集使歸郡應制 (Feng he sheng zhi mu chun song chao ji shi gui jun ying zhi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
萬國仰宗周，衣冠拜冕旒。
玉乘迎大客，金節送諸侯。
祖席傾三省，褰帷向九州。
楊花飛上路，槐色蔭通溝。
來預鈞天樂，歸分漢主憂。
宸章類河漢，垂象滿中州。

poems.title: 奉和聖製重陽節宰臣及羣官上壽應制 (Feng he sheng zhi zhong yang jie zai chen ji qun guan shang shou ying zhi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
四海方無事，三秋大有年。
百生無此日，萬壽願齊天。
芍藥和金鼎，茱萸插玳筵。
玉堂開右个，天樂動宮懸。
御柳疎秋景，城鴉拂曙煙。
無窮菊花節，長奉柏梁篇。

poems.title: 奉和聖製十五夜然燈繼以酺宴應制 (Feng he sheng zhi shi wu ye ran deng ji yi pu yan ying zhi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
上路笙歌滿，春城漏刻長。
遊人多晝日，明月讓燈光。
魚鑰通翔鳳，龍輿出建章。
九衢陳廣樂，百福透名香。
仙伎來金殿，都人遶玉堂。
定應偷妙舞，從此學新妝。
奉引迎三事，司儀列萬方。
願將天地壽，同以獻君王。

poems.title: 奉和聖製幸玉真公主山莊因題石壁十韻之作應制 (Feng he sheng zhi xing yu zhen gong zhu shan zhuang yin ti shi bi shi yun zhi zuo ying zhi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
碧落風煙外，瑤臺道路賒。
如何連帝苑，別自有仙家。
此地回鸞駕，緣谿轉翠華。
洞中開日月，窗裏發雲霞。
庭養沖天鶴，溪流上漢查。
種田生白玉，泥竈化丹砂。
谷靜泉逾響，山深日易斜。
御羹和石髓，香飯進胡麻。
大道今無外，長生詎有涯。
還瞻九霄上，來往五雲車。

poems.title: 和僕射晉公扈從溫湯 (He pu ye jin gong hu cong wen tang)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
天子幸新豐，旌旗渭水東。
寒山天仗外，溫谷幔城中。
奠玉羣仙座，焚香太乙宮。
出遊逢牧馬，罷獵見非熊。
上宰無爲化，明時太古同。
靈芝三秀紫，陳粟萬箱紅。
王禮奠儒教，天兵小戰功。
謀猶歸哲匠，詞賦屬文宗。
司諫方無闕，陳詩且未工。
長吟吉甫頌，朝夕仰清風。

poems.title: 贈東嶽焦鍊師 (Zeng dong yue jiao lian shi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
先生千歲餘，五嶽遍曾居。
遙識齊侯鼎，新過王母廬。
不能師孔墨，何事問長沮。
玉管時來鳳，銅盤即釣魚。
竦身空裏語，明目夜中書。
自有還丹術，時論太素初。
頻蒙露版詔，時降軟輪車。
山靜泉逾響，松高枝轉疎。
搘頤問樵客，世上復何如。

poems.title: 送祕書晁監還日本國 (Song mi shu chao jian huan ri ben guo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
積水不可極，安知滄海東。
九州何處遠，萬里若乘空。
向國唯看日，歸帆但信風。
鰲身暎天黑，魚眼射波紅。
鄉樹扶桑外，主人孤島中。
別離方異域，音信若爲通。

poems.title: 送李太守赴上洛 (Song li tai shou fu shang luo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
商山包楚鄧，積翠藹沈沈。
驛路飛泉灑，關門落照深。
野花開古戍，行客響空林。
板屋春多雨，山城晝欲陰。
丹泉通虢略，白羽抵荆岑。
若見西山爽，應知黃綺心。

poems.title: 春過賀遂員外藥園 (Chun guo he sui yuan wai yao yuan)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
前年槿籬故，新作藥欄成。
香草爲君子，名花是長卿。
水穿盤石透，藤繫古松生。
畫畏開廚走，來蒙到屣迎。
蔗漿菰米飯，蒟醬露葵羹。
頗識灌園意，於陵不自輕。

poems.title: 遊感化寺 (You gan hua si)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
翡翠香煙合，琉璃寶地平。
龍宮連棟宇，虎穴傍檐楹。
谷靜唯松響，山深無鳥聲。
瓊峰當戶拆，金澗透林明。
郢路雲端逈，秦川雨外晴。
鴈王銜果獻，鹿女踏花行。
抖擻辭貧里，歸依宿化城。
繞籬生野蕨，空館發山櫻。
香飯青菰米，嘉蔬綠笋莖。
誓陪清梵末，端坐學無生。

poems.title: 遊悟真寺 (You wu zhen si)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
聞道黃金地，仍開白玉田。
擲山移巨石，呪嶺出飛泉。
猛虎同三逕，愁猿學四禪。
買香然綠桂，乞火踏紅蓮。
草色搖霞上，松聲汎月邊。
山河窮百二，世界接三千。
梵宇聊憑視，王城遂渺然。
灞陵纔出樹，渭水欲連天。
遠縣分諸郭，孤村起白煙。
望雲思聖主，披霧隱羣賢。
薄宦慚尸素，終身擬尚玄。
誰知草菴客，曾和柏梁篇。

poems.title: 曉行巴峽 (Xiao xing ba xia)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
際曉投巴峽，餘春憶帝京。
晴江一女浣，朝日衆雞鳴。
水國舟中市，山橋樹杪行。
登高萬井出，眺迥二流明。
人作殊方語，鸎爲故國聲。
賴多山水趣，稍解別離情。

poems.title: 田家 (Tian jia)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
舊穀行將盡，良苗未可希。
老年方愛粥，卒歲且無衣。
雀乳青苔井，雞鳴白板扉。
柴車駕羸牸，草屩牧豪狶。
夕雨紅榴拆，新秋綠芋肥。
餉田桑下憩，旁舍草中歸。
住處名愚谷，何煩問是非。

poems.title: 大同殿柱產玉芝龍池上有慶雲神光照殿百官共覩聖恩便賜宴樂敢書即事 (Da tong dian zhu chan yu zhi long chi shang you qing yun shen guang zhao dian bai guan gong du sheng en bian ci yan le gan shu ji shi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
欲笑周文歌宴鎬，遙輕漢武樂橫汾。
豈知玉殿生三秀，詎有銅池出五雲。
陌上堯樽傾北斗，樓前舜樂動南薰。
共歡天意同人意，萬歲千秋奉聖君。

poems.title: 敕賜百官櫻桃 (Chi ci bai guan ying tao)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
芙蓉闕下會千官，紫禁朱櫻出上蘭。
纔是寢園春薦後，非關御苑鳥銜殘。
歸鞍競帶青絲籠，中使頻傾赤玉盤。
飽食不須愁內熱，大官還有蔗漿寒。

poems.title: 敕借岐王九成宮避暑應教 (Chi jie qi wang jiu cheng gong bi shu ying jiao)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
帝子遠辭丹鳳闕，天書遙借翠微宮。
隔窗雲霧生衣上，卷幔山泉入鏡中。
林下水聲喧語笑，巖間樹色隱房櫳。
仙家未必能勝此，何事吹笙向碧空。

poems.title: 和太常韋主簿五郎溫湯寓目之作 (He tai chang wei zhu bu wu lang wen tang yu mu zhi zuo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
漢主離宮接露臺，秦川一半夕陽開。
青山盡是朱旗繞，碧澗翻從玉殿來。
新豐樹裏行人度，小苑城邊獵騎廻。
聞道甘泉能獻賦，懸知獨有子雲才。

poems.title: 出塞 (Chu sai)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
居延城外獵天驕，白草連天野火燒。
暮雲空磧時驅馬，秋日平原好射鵰。
護羌校尉朝乘障，破虜將軍夜渡遼。
玉靶角弓珠勒馬，漢家將賜霍嫖姚。

poems.title: 送楊少府貶郴州 (Song yang shao fu bian chen zhou)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
明到衡山與洞庭，若爲秋月聽猿聲。
愁看北渚三湘遠，惡說南風五兩輕。
青草瘴時過夏口，白頭浪裏出湓城。
長沙不久留才子，賈誼何須弔屈平。

poems.title: 過乘如禪師蕭居士嵩丘蘭若 (Guo cheng ru chan shi xiao ju shi song qiu lan ruo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
無着天親弟與兄，嵩丘蘭若一峰晴。
食隨鳴磬巢烏下，行踏空林落葉聲。
迸水定侵香案濕，雨花應共石牀平。
深洞長松何所有，儼然天竺古先生。

poems.title: 春日與裴迪過新昌里訪呂逸人不遇 (Chun ri yu pei di guo xin chang li fang lü yi ren bu yu)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
桃源一向絕風塵，柳市南頭訪隱淪。
到門不敢題凡鳥，看竹何須問主人。
城上青山如屋裏，東家流水入西鄰。
閉戶著書多歲月，種松皆老作龍鱗。

poems.title: 酌酒與裴迪 (Zhuo jiu yu pei di)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
酌酒與君君自寬，人情翻覆似波瀾。
白首相知猶按劒，朱門先達笑彈冠。
草色全經細雨濕，花枝欲動春風寒。
世事浮雲何足問，不如高臥且加餐。

poems.title: 早秋山中作 (Zao qiu shan zhong zuo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
無才不敢累明時，思向東谿守故籬。
豈厭尚平婚嫁早，却嫌陶令去官遲。
草間蛩響臨秋急，山裏蟬聲薄暮悲。
寂寞柴門人不到，空林獨與白雲期。

poems.title: 息夫人 (Xi fu ren)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
莫以今時寵，難忘舊日恩。
看花滿眼淚，不共楚王言。

poems.title: 班倢伃三首·其二 (Ban jie yu san shou, qi er)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
宮殿生秋草，君王恩幸疎。
那堪聞鳳吹，門外度金輿。

poems.title: 輞川集·華子岡 (Wang chuan ji, hua zi gang)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
飛鳥去不窮，連山復秋色。
上下華子岡，惆悵情何極。

poems.title: 輞川集·文杏館 (Wang chuan ji, wen xing guan)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
文杏裁爲梁，香茅結爲宇。
不知棟裏雲，去作人間雨。

poems.title: 輞川集·柳浪 (Wang chuan ji, liu lang)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
分行接綺樹，倒影入清漪。
不學御溝上，春風傷別離。

poems.title: 輞川集·白石灘 (Wang chuan ji, bai shi tan)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
清淺白石灘，綠蒲向堪把。
家住水東西，浣紗明月下。

poems.title: 輞川集·辛夷塢 (Wang chuan ji, xin yi wu)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
木末芙蓉花，山中發紅萼。
澗戶寂無人，紛紛開且落。

poems.title: 輞川集·漆園 (Wang chuan ji, qi yuan)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
古人非傲吏，自闕經世務。
偶寄一微官，婆娑數株樹。

poems.title: 荅裴迪輞口遇雨憶終南山之作 (Da pei di wang kou yu yu yi zhong nan shan zhi zuo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
淼淼寒流廣，蒼蒼秋雨晦。
君問終南山，心知白雲外。

poems.title: 山中寄諸弟妹 (Shan zhong ji zhu di mei)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
山中多法侶，禪誦自爲羣。
城郭遙相望，唯應見白雲。

poems.title: 班倢伃三首·其三 (Ban jie yu san shou, qi san)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
怪來妝閣閉，朝下不相迎。
總向春園裏，花間語笑聲。

poems.title: 臨高臺送黎拾遺 (Lin gao tai song li shi yi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
相送臨高臺，川原杳何極。
日暮飛鳥還，行人去不息。

poems.title: 崔九弟欲往南山馬上口號與別 (Cui jiu di yu wang nan shan ma shang kou hao yu bie)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
城隅一分手，幾日還相見。
山中有桂花，莫待花如霰。

poems.title: 雜詩三首·其一 (Za shi san shou, qi yi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
家住孟津河，門對孟津口。
常有江南船，寄書家中否。

poems.title: 雜詩三首·其三 (Za shi san shou, qi san)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
已見寒梅發，復聞啼鳥聲。
心心視春草，畏向階前生。

poems.title: 闕題二首·其一 (Que ti er shou, qi yi)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
荆谿白石出，天寒紅葉稀。
山路元無雨，空翠濕人衣。

poems.title: 田園樂七首·其三 (Tian yuan le qi shou, qi san)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
采菱渡頭風急，策杖林西日斜。
杏樹壇邊漁父，桃花源裏人家。

poems.title: 田園樂七首·其四 (Tian yuan le qi shou, qi si)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
萋萋春草秋綠，落落長松夏寒。
牛羊自歸村巷，童稚不識衣冠。

poems.title: 田園樂七首·其五 (Tian yuan le qi shou, qi wu)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
山下孤煙遠村，天邊獨樹高原。
一瓢顏回陋巷，五柳先生對門。

poems.title: 渡河到清河作 (Du he dao qing he zuo)
poems.author: Wang Wei
poems.text:
汎舟大河裏，積水窮天涯。
天波忽開拆，郡邑千萬家。
行復見城市，宛然有桑麻。
回瞻舊鄉國，淼漫連雲霞。
